# Fathom dogfood journal: app-kit

Date:2026-09-16. Audience: the next Fathom development session.
Scope: app-kit work plus its explicitly scoped consumer pilots. This is a source-
grounded agent assessment, not a controlled productivity experiment or release review.

## Verdict

**Keep Fathom, but use it selectively.** Exact code navigation, continuity and structured
failure intake are useful. Broad retrieval, stale obligation citations and inconsistent
measurement identity create real friction. I judge it worthwhile as a focused companion,
not yet as a universal mandatory discovery layer or a trustworthy narrator of its own
ROI in this session. Net time/token savings are **not established**.

The largest next win is tighter identity/freshness/bounded-output behavior, not more
tools. Tool existence, authored guards and a green schema are not demonstrated impact.

## What helped, and what did not

| Area | Concrete observation | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Exact navigation | `find_symbol` located Catalog across four owning packages and Gate in `internal/designreceipts/check.go`, with verified paths/lines. | Useful for precise where/what questions; still inspect source for consequential edits. |
| Continuity | `fathom thread brief` restored the exact private-candidate receipt, retained failures, pending authority and RAC ownership after compaction. | Valuable handoff content; long open-thread backlogs need pruning and task relevance. |
| Scope and proof | `plans status` separates45 proven legacy rows,6 open experience rows and11 deferred rows. | Useful static-plan distinction, not UI, native, runtime or consumer acceptance. |
| Configuration contracts | Current `config audit`:4 hold,0 violated/unable/off;26 pointers resolve and advertised stanza tools are served. | A bounded current check, not proof that both agent hosts obey instructions. |
| Failure intake |25 local observations exist after this review; source/exclusion and guidance defects have recorded repairs. | Real reusable feedback; unresolved repetitions need triage instead of new duplicate entries. |
| Broad/ambiguous retrieval | O12 reports a63k-token unresolved Run context; O22 a53k-token package-like lookup; O23 unrelated intent-check results. | Output budgets and no-match behavior must be server-enforced. Earlier reports are historical, not re-executed here. |
| Governing rules | After successful ingest, obligations still cite stale CLAUDE lines at watermark `6bf5e4b…`. | A warning label does not make stale content safe to present as binding. Read current intent instead. |
| Service identity | Earlier consumer work repeatedly resolved Fathom to a scratch clone rather than the authorized paused checkout. | Correct name with wrong checkout is a dangerous near-match. Identity must precede discovery. |
| Runtime quality | Go/race, browser, native, CSS and private-delivery probes found real defects. | Those are their own instruments. Do not attribute the CSV/schema, focus or layout catches to Fathom without evidence. |

Some waste was **my usage**, not a Fathom defect: an overly broad repo map, printing
both MCP text and structured content, and grep through large hash inventories inflated
context. Prefer exact queries, bounded package maps and only `structuredContent` when
available. Do not claim that avoiding my own inefficient queries measures Fathom ROI.

## Prioritized Fathom improvements and acceptance tests

| Priority | Improvement | Proof to require |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | One service/checkout/session/log identity across MCP, CLI, hooks and reports | Write a known local synthetic call; every instrument resolves the same root/run and sees it. Mismatched/absent input says unknown, not zero. |
| P0 | Withhold stale obligations from authoritative injection | Move the source rule, ingest/recompile, then verify rule hash/snippet/watermark; stale results are nonbinding diagnostics with one precise remedy. |
| P1 | Bounded ambiguous queries and typed confidence | Unresolved Run/gallery returns short candidates, not cross-service floods; enforce byte/result caps and exclude binaries. |
| P1 | Semantic shared loaders for capabilities and doctor | Quoted CUE labels, missing, invalid and unreadable files yield the same guard/module verdict on every surface. |
| P1 | Working-tree and service-root freshness | Untracked edited Go/.mjs symbols either resolve after refresh or report parser/root limitations explicitly; HEAD freshness alone is insufficient. |
| P2 | Lean task-specific orientation | One compact identity+next-action capsule; dedupe already-served rules, rank open threads, separate semantic code search from literal/document search. |
| P2 | Credible impact experiment | Same repo/session population, matched workload and cost accounting, adequate ON/OFF units; keep calls/cost/catches distinct from causal savings. |

Do not expand the MCP surface merely to make these reports greener. Reuse existing
receipt/pact concepts and make each command agree about the data it is describing.
No daemon reroot, deployment, hook repair, global rating or Fathom source mutation was
performed for this journal. O25 was filed locally; triage it with the existing identity
issues rather than applying an unreviewed global fix.
